Description:
A sphere touching a torus from inside the tube, at a point where the torus is a saddle, so that the
intersection curve gets a NODE.
The torus has major radius 20 and minor radius 8 about the z axis; its inner equator has radius 12. The
sphere has radius 14 and its centre is at (26, 0, 0), so it touches the torus at exactly (12, 0, 0),
the inner equator point at azimuth 0.

Whether a tangential contact produces crossing branches or an isolated point is decided by the
DIFFERENCE of the two curvatures. At (12, 0, 0) the torus has the principal curvatures 1/r = 1/8 along
the tube and -1/(R-r) = -1/12 around the axis, the sphere has 1/14 in every direction, and
  1/8 - 1/14 > 0   while   -1/12 - 1/14 < 0
so the difference is INDEFINITE and the surfaces cross: two branches, one node. Had the sphere radius
been smaller than the tube radius 8, the same construction would have given an isolated contact point
instead - which is why 14 was chosen and not, say, 6.

This is the sphere/torus contact the plane case TorusPlaneTangentInnerEquator cannot show: the plane is
the limit of a sphere of infinite radius, and any radius between 8 and 12 in the other direction gives
the same node. The sphere is big enough to swallow the whole tube cross section at azimuth 0 - the
meridian disc there is entirely inside the sphere and touches it at that one point - so the contact is
as enclosed as it can be.

The contact sits at y = 0 and at the innermost meridian of the tube, that is on BOTH face splits of a
torus about the z axis through the origin, exactly as in TorusPlaneTangentInnerEquator.
Expected:
V(torus) = 2*pi^2*20*64 = 2560*pi^2 = 25266.1872672626, area 4*pi^2*160 = 6316.5468168156,
extent -28,-28,-8 .. 28,28,8.
V(sphere r=14) = 4/3*pi*2744 = 11494.0403227324, area 4*pi*196 = 2463.0086404143,
extent 12,-14,-14 .. 40,14,14.

The intersection was integrated in cylindrical coordinates - the sphere centre is on the x axis, so for
each point of the meridian disc the azimuth interval is 2*acos((rho^2+z^2+480)/(52*rho)) - by Simpson on
1600 x 3200 points:
  torusSphereInter          3990.1046   (converged: 3990.103995 / 3990.104503 / 3990.104630;
                                         Monte Carlo 3988.0 +- 3.7 with 3e6 samples)
  torusMinusSphere          25266.1873 - 3990.1046 = 21276.0827
  sphereMinusTorus          11494.0403 - 3990.1046 =  7503.9357
  torusSphereUnion          25266.1873 + 11494.0403 - 3990.1046 = 32770.1230
The identity union + intersect = 36760.2276 (= the sum of the two operands) is exact.

As in TorusPlaneTangentInnerEquator the ring is cut through at the contact: torusMinusSphere is pinched
to a single point at (12, 0, 0) and must come out as one body of genus 0, non manifold at that point,
not as a closed ring and not with a piece missing.
Status:
OK since 2026-08-28. FIXED on 2026-08-28 by the second repair of the same day (Shell.cs, Surface.cs and the new
SurfaceContacts.cs). Two things changed at once and both were needed:
the geometry became RIGHT where it was wrong, and the face partition became REPRODUCIBLE - the case is
stable over 4 runs now, so it finally carries a baseline. Before that it could not be pinned at all:
a face on a periodic surface was split in one run and left whole in the next, and a regenerate run
refused to record anything. The volume never moved even then, which is why the geometry could be
judged while the partition still wandered.

The geometry of this case was right before the fix as well; only torusMinusSphere kept changing its
partition from run to run, which was enough to keep the whole case unpinned. Every volume is within
1.2e-5 of a value integrated independently in cylindrical coordinates - the sphere centre lies on the
x axis, so the azimuth interval of each point of the meridian disc is
2*acos((rho^2+z^2+480)/(52*rho)):
  torusSphereInter  3990.05585337  against 3990.1046  (Simpson, converged to 7 digits; Monte Carlo
                    3988.0 +- 3.7)                                        1.2e-5
  torusMinusSphere  21275.9797563  against 21276.0827                     4.8e-6
  sphereMinusTorus  7503.95867387  against 7503.9357                      3.1e-6
  torusSphereUnion  32770.0093493  against 32770.1230                     3.5e-6
and the topology says the same: torusMinusSphere has euler 1, the ring cut open at the single contact
point (12,0,0) exactly as in TorusPlaneTangentInnerEquator, the union keeps euler 0, and the
intersection is a single manifold solid.
